papers.title: Visitor's diary
lines: Took the waters, which taste of warm pennies. Danced at the Assembly. Trod on a Lord.
He was very civil about it, and his foot has since recovered.

papers.title: Barn door note
lines: The cider is in the third barrel, not the second, whatever Pete tells you.
The second barrel is for the pigs. They love it. They sing.

papers.title: Farmer's letter
lines: The ponies are out on the moor and will not be told. They have been on Dartmoor since before there were farmers.
If a grey one follows you home, feed her. She'll stay till she gets bored.

trail.clue: A farmer hid a coin purse near the old oak on the moor, 'where the ponies won't dig'.

papers.title: Shipwright's note
lines: The great iron ship is to be launched on the tide. Nobody believes she will float. Nobody dares say it aloud.
The Captain has bet a week's pay she will. He has also hidden a spare week in the lining of his hat.

papers.title: Pilgrim's card
lines: Climbed the Tor in the dawn. Saw mist, a crow, and a man in a cloak with a tin whistle.
Whether he is a druid or on his way to a fete, I did not ask.

trail.clue: A pilgrim left a charm in the grass near the big rock, as pilgrims do.

papers.title: Notice to mariners
lines: All able seamen are requested to attend the Admiral's table. Attendance is required. Refusal is discouraged.
Rum will be served. There is no further reason to attend.

papers.title: Tearoom argument
lines: The cream goes on the jam, not the jam on the cream. This is the Devon way and it is not up for discussion.
A note below, in Cornish handwriting: 'We shall see about that.'
